assets.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a single seamless-looking wide distant background layer for an orthographic 2D pixel art industrial bunker defense videogame. Create ONLY the distant outdoor skyline and sky: smoky dark blue-gray cloud banks above a subdued dusty coral sunset horizon, distant ruined industrial towers and smokestacks, layers of tiny dark city silhouettes fading into haze. Gritty detailed late-1990s hand-painted pixel-art appearance with visible crisp pixels, limited desaturated charcoal, navy, slate, dull muted rust palette. Wide landscape 3:1 composition, skyline along bottom quarter, cloud sky fills upper three quarters. Front-most bottom silhouettes nearly black. Deliberately subdued, dark enough that warm lights in foreground gameplay will stand out. No bunker, no interior, no foreground platforms, no ground cross-section, no characters, no machines, no robots, no vehicles, no weapons, no text, no interface, no logos. This will sit behind real separately animated gameplay geometry.

Use case stylized-concept. Create a production game asset: ONLY the recessed background wall of an old underground concrete bunker, for a gritty orthographic 2D side-view pixel art game. Wide panoramic horizontal image 3:1. Rich detailed hand-crafted late-1990s pixel-art aesthetics, crisp small pixel clusters, weathered gray concrete blocks, chipped corners, dark fissures, tiny rust stains, industrial olive-gray electrical conduit and a few thin copper pipes, subtly stained panels. Warm amber low work-light washing the upper wall and faint light cones downwards, very dark lower corners. Entire image is flat straight-on elevation of one continuous empty back wall. A thin pipe bundle along the upper edge, some vertically down left edge. Keep the center and bottom empty of objects so real separately drawn animated workers and machines can be placed in front. Muted desaturated charcoal, gray, olive, dull brown, subtle amber light. No text, no UI, no characters, no machines, no floor, no ceiling, no doors, no furniture, no windows, no perspective, no exterior view. Detailed environment wall material, dramatic but readable, no flat vector shapes. This is a background material layer for a separately built playable bunker, not a complete game scene.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: seamless repeating 2D tile material for a gritty underground bunker pixel art game. Square texture, completely filled with tightly interlocking dark irregular basalt rubble and almost-black soil, coarse rounded fractured stones outlined with deep shadows, occasional tiny brown seams of earth. Side-view subterranean rock cross-section wall, flat surface with no perspective. Detailed classic hand-pixeled game aesthetic, crisp restrained pixel clusters, charcoal and very dark muted brown palette with sparse gray edge highlights. The rocks vary from small pebbles to fist sized, consistent natural dense geology. Dark enough as background around lit bunker cutaways. No isolated objects, no gaps, no crystals, no ores, no text, no UI, no characters, no cave openings, no buildings, no machinery. Material texture only, uniform lighting, edges should tile seamlessly.

animation_and_sounds: Original worker pixel pose atlases (19 states, 110 poses per palette), distance-synchronized ladder animation and separate GDScript animation for eighteen enemy classes, weapons, modular production machinery, expansion rooms, effects and weather. Generated enemy and machinery components remain separately replaceable. Original synthesized music and layered sounds; no third-party game assets.

runtime_art.usage: Six separately animated mechanical chassis, hydraulic legs and weapons: runner, strider, breaker, assault, colossus and siege. Generated body art is documented in enemies/source.json; behavior, gait, recoil and telegraph timing are original GDScript.
Original drawn rifle, shotgun and impulse weapon, projectiles, muzzle flashes and recoil. Gameplay collision remains separate from art.
Original cold-glowing machine-core pickups are automatically absorbed as shared upgrade points. They do not occupy worker inventory or use the held-material sprite atlas.

Four physical front-wall tiers remain available. The previous fixed-layout underground shafts, six rooms and separately paid wall lining are retained for legacy fixtures through game.start(). They are not the room flow of the normal menu start; the scenario architecture below supplies that flow.

Original GDScript pixel silhouettes for the field workbench, articulated steel jaws, explosive mine, kit cargo and placement previews. Crafted manual guns reuse the existing independently animated RoofTurret assets.
Original steel/composite armor plates and muted character patches follow anchor positions for the existing 110 worker poses. Existing body and foreground arm textures are unchanged.

Mother Machine reuses the documented siege chassis, adding original animated drive, riveted crown and antennae. Character selection, XP, achievements and boss transmissions reuse the existing UI texture/font and worker/enemy atlases; no third-party game assets.

Original code-drawn shields, lance, long barrel, demolition hammer, repair equipment and cooling armor on six new ground variants. Reuses the documented original six generated chassis; no new third-party assets.

Six original airborne mechanical assemblies reuse small documented chassis-atlas regions with separately drawn animated rotors, wings, thrusters, shields, weapons and swept projectiles. Original GDScript geometry, not six new hand-painted raster atlases.

Original riveted tower, bunker console, ladder and three upgrade-stage details; reuses existing turret components and separate recoil/muzzle animation. Dome service opening is rendered from the same polygons used for collision.

Four original idle gestures and articulated wounded, treatment, collapse and rising poses. Runtime GDScript reuses unmodified head/helmet and jacket atlas regions; limbs use the exact original worker palette and anatomy. Persistent dressing/splint marks and bounded blood drops follow actual medical state. No new raster assets or third-party game artwork.

Original separately animated olive/steel rescue automaton, articulated medical tool, tread and ladder motion, and small pixel dressing/splint HUD marks. Native Godot drawing, separate navigation and medical logic; not a painted sprite sheet.

Original three-layer pixel rain with swept first-contact physics. Existing texture alpha is read-only sampled for weather outlines that follow props, gun recoil, animated flag and actor equipment. No raster file edits, new third-party graphics, or gameplay collision changes.

Original runtime damp-material shader, articulated dripping, supported damp strips, material-aware rain splashes and muddy footprints. Uses existing atlas colors/transparency and actual animation anchors. Dry/wet preview states are arranged in Godot; main-scene preview uses real rain accumulation and normal InputMap movement.

Original modular Godot architecture: one inhabited starting room, one raw mining gallery and four individually paid, curing expansions. Three construction types combine the generated wall materials with separately drawn structural frames, platforms, warm lamps, contacts and shafts. Shared room definitions determine costs, wave unlocks, stations and one-time core bonuses. Game geometry, actor paths and collisions remain independent of the images.

Original runtime panorama composition, individually masked sky motion, two drifting transparent cloud depths and chimney-anchored smoke. Buildings, cranes and mountains remain stationary. Background image palette and anchor data are environment-specific.

Original pre-game selection uses the documented generated panorama thumbnails, existing metal UI texture and font. West, center and east layouts use actual world-space geometry and directed enemy routes; centered placement splits the same enemy total across two fronts. No external game assets.
